comment: Owned by M5b. Forecast-curve accuracy, distinct from thresholds/full_output.json. The ceiling ratchets DOWN when a change is accepted and is never raised to accommodate a regression.

history.note: The harness's own starting point: predicting no drawdown at all is 100% error on every exact sample. Recorded so the first real forecaster has something to beat.

history.forecaster: build_explicit (explicit future events only, no recurrence projection)
history.note: The explicit-only baseline. The median is unchanged from the zero forecaster because 15 of the 25 samples - and 14 of the 21 exact ones - have no explicit future events at all, so their curve is flat and their drawdown is zero by construction. The mean moves from 100% to 94.21%, which is the whole contribution of every pending debit and scheduled row in the dataset. That gap is the measured size of the projection job M7b has to do: on most samples, all of it.

history.forecaster: build (explicit events + recurring projection, safety horizon at desired_completion_date)
history.note: Three changes, each measured separately. Projection alone: median 100% -> 16.4%. De-duplicating a projected occurrence against the explicit scheduled row that already covers it, keyed on (direction, category) rather than on description: 16.4% -> 14.8%, almost all of it request_13, whose scheduled salary is described differently from the history it continues. Seeding a monthly series from a scheduled credit with no detectable history (PLAN assumption 4): fixed request_01's upper-bound violation, 31,418 predicted against a 15,225 bound, down to 10,209. Measuring the trough through desired_completion_date instead of the full 90-day window: mean 67.6% -> 32.1% and the last bound violation gone; the median did not move, which is what says it is a tail correction and not a re-fit.

history.forecaster: build, with the calibrated estimator: expenses at the 75th percentile of the last 6 observations, income at the mean of the last 6, MIN_OCCURRENCES 3 relaxed to 2 for an all-identical series
history.note: Two accepted changes. (1) Expense series move from the mean of recent observations to the 75th percentile, which is what the spec's 'forecast essential variable spending conservatively' asks for: median 14.54% -> 11.25%, mean 29.66% -> 28.97%, within-25% 16 of 21. Income stays at the mean. (2) MIN_OCCURRENCES relaxed from 3 to 2 when every recorded amount in the series is identical, which lets user_15's twice-paid EUR 1,661 first-job payroll project while still refusing user_11's IDR 20.0M-then-8.5M commission. Neither change touches a three-or-more-occurrence series, so the variance gate PLAN.md 5.5 rules out stays out.

rejected_variants.variant: Step monthly series by their median gap from the last occurrence instead of anchoring to the modal day-of-month
rejected_variants.note: Confirms the planning finding on the corrected forecaster. Phase beats amount: drifting a monthly series by a day or two per cycle moves the trough across a salary date.

rejected_variants.variant: Project no income at all; count only the explicitly scheduled rows
rejected_variants.note: A defensible reading of 'do not invent unsupported future income', and catastrophic. Recurring salary is projected; which series qualify is the question, and that is what the M6 gate answers.

rejected_variants.variant: Maximum of recent observations for every series, income included
rejected_variants.note: Over-states income, which the spec forbids. It measures better only because it rescues request_08, whose salary runs EUR 1,422.85 four times then 782.57 and whose correct forward amount is stated in a message - that belongs to the evidence layer, not to a statistic that happens to land on it. Also loses a within-25% sample.

rejected_variants.variant: Maximum of recent observations for expenses only
rejected_variants.note: Worse than p75 on all three figures; the blanket-max finding from planning survives at the top of the range even though a high percentile does not.

rejected_variants.variant: 90th percentile of recent observations for expenses
rejected_variants.note: Marginally better median than p75, worse mean and one fewer sample within 25%. Not worth the extra conservatism.

Projects user_11's 'Monthly sales commission' from two occurrences, which a message says is unapproved. The number improves because an over-credited commission cancels an over-forecast elsewhere; the semantics are wrong and PLAN.md 5.5 names this exact series as one that must not project.

rejected_variants.variant: Income at the minimum, or at the single last observation, of recent history
rejected_variants.note: Both roughly 42% mean error. Under-stating income is not free conservatism: it invents a shortfall and suppresses affordability.

rejected_variants.variant: Fixed 90-day safety horizon instead of the request's desired_completion_date
rejected_variants.note: Kept here because it is the single largest tail effect found. See the M7b history entry.

rejected_variants.variant: Cadence limited to a fixed weekly/fortnightly/monthly menu

measured.note: Rejected 280 debit series across the dataset that are perfectly regular at 5, 10 or 21 days

rejected_variants.note: Silently dropped real recurring spending from every affected forecast.
